radiation: Invisible energy rays and high-speed particles from the Sun and deep space that can harm human bodies and sensitive electronic circuits.
sol: A solar day on Mars, lasting 24 hours, 39 minutes, and 35 seconds, which is just slightly longer than an Earth day.
solar flare: A sudden burst of light and other radiation from the Sun. It can disturb radio signals and spacecraft.
shielding: Material placed between people and space radiation to lower their exposure.
comm delay: The lag time required for radio communication signals travelling at the speed of light to cross the vast space between Earth and other worlds.
microgravity: The state of apparent weightlessness experienced by astronauts and spacecraft when they are in free fall in orbit.
life support: Equipment that provides clean air and water and keeps a space home safe for people.
oxygen: A gas people need to breathe.
carbon dioxide: A gas people breathe out. Too much of it in a closed cabin makes the air unsafe.
scrubber: A machine or filter that removes carbon dioxide from cabin air.
airlock: A small chamber with doors that lets astronauts move between a pressurized habitat and outside.
habitat: A place where astronauts can live and work safely.
regolith: Loose dust and broken rock covering the Moon or Mars.
micrometeoroid: A tiny bit of space rock or dust moving through space.
dust devil: A spinning column of dust lifted by moving air.
dust storm: A storm that lifts dust into the air and can dim sunlight.
lunar night: The dark part of a Moon day. Away from the poles, it lasts about 14 Earth days.
solar panel: A device that turns sunlight into electricity.
solar array: A group of solar panels that makes electricity from sunlight.
perchlorates: Salts found in Martian soil that can be harmful to living things.
cosmic rays: Fast particles from beyond our solar system that can add to astronauts’ radiation exposure.
hydroponic: A way to grow plants with water and nutrients instead of ordinary soil.
solar conjunction: A time when Mars appears close to the Sun from Earth, making radio messages harder to send.
